content: Round 2026-11-10: niriWayle daily-driver completion — aports NEW hyprsunset 0.4.0-r0 (edge-testing port, tag-pinned; wayle r1 depends += hyprsunset so the night-light toggle works), NEW xdg-desktop-portal-gnome 999 EMPTY shadow-dummy (niri-portalsconf dep resolves to it -> nautilus + mutter backend never install; gtk+wlr keep portals per verbatim .portal Interfaces evidence), NEW file-roller-user-dinit (2 activation names, 1 unit) + evince-user-dinit (evinced), RETIRED xdg-desktop-portal-gnome-user-dinit, ursine 0.27.0-r0 depends parted/shadow/util-linux (no-D-Bus release: useradd/chpasswd + mount/blkid CLI, zbus dropped) -> accountsservice + udisks2 leave the install; feralos: niriWayle += dconf evince file-roller gnome-firmware gnome-maps thunderbird obs-studio gst-libav (H.265, only missing gst decoder) font-noto-emoji, -= khal + dupes (dbus/firewalld/xdg-user-dirs/font-terminus also from niri); installer seeds FULL user portals conf (default=gtk + wlr screenshot/screencast + Secret pins); harness live-activation target UDisks2 -> org.freedesktop.Avahi. Commits aports 2d5ea4b, feralos 216e77f.

Shadow-dummy pattern (less-dummy style): an EMPTY aports package with the SAME pkgname as an Alpine one and pkgver 999 beats every upstream version — apk resolves the dependency chain against it and the real package never installs. Used for xdg-desktop-portal-gnome (dep of Alpine's niri-portalsconf; the real one drags nautilus + mutter backend). Upgrade-safe: plain apk upgrade never downgrades. Prefer this over installer-side providePackages when the shadow should live in the repo.

xdg-desktop-portal backend coverage on Alpine (verbatim from .portal files): gtk = FileChooser AppChooser Print Notification Inhibit Access Account Email DynamicLauncher Lockdown Settings Wallpaper; wlr = Screenshot ScreenCast; gnome adds only RemoteDesktop GlobalShortcuts (plus dupes). Secret is served by gnome-keyring/oo7 own .portal files, NOT the backends. So gtk+wlr fully replace the gnome backend for a wlroots-adjacent desktop.
